prompt: A reviewer found these problems in your research questions and plan. Fix each one, keeping every rule for questions and plan: don't give a side equipment or dat

content.text:
Let me fix the two issues and return only researchQuestions, plan, and candidate.

Fix 1: In Phase 2, state the company procures a portable oxygen analyser (company procurement, no record contradicts this as a purchase decision).

Fix 2: Narrow RQ1 to autoxidation vs. photo-oxidation only, since the available markers (PV, p-AV, TBARS, fatty acid profile, tocopherol, Rancimat) can distinguish these but not enzymatic or trace-metal pathways.

{"researchQuestions":["Which pathway—autoxidation or photo-oxidation—accounts for the dominant share of peroxide accumulation across production batches, measured against fatty acid composition, tocopherol content, p-anisidine value, and Rancimat induction period data from the same batches?","What is the residual headspace oxygen concentration achieved by the current nitrogen flush, measured against the 2% threshold defined in published filling-line specifications?","Do process changes to the nitrogen flush or storage temperature reduce the rate of peroxide accumulation to levels consistent with a 9-month shelf life, measured against peroxide value trajectories from untreated control bottles held in parallel?"],"plan":[{"phase":"Phase 1 – Baseline characterisation (months 1–2)","work":"University lab runs GC-FID fatty acid profiling, HPLC-FLD tocopherol quantification, and Rancimat induction period on fresh oil samples prepared by the company lab technician across three recent batches.","result":"A baseline dataset of fatty acid composition, tocopherol content, and oxidative stability index for three batches, delivered as a data report."},{"phase":"Phase 2 – Pathway identification (months 3–5)","work":"University lab measures peroxide value, p-anisidine value, and TBARS on time-series samples stored at two temperatures. Company procures a portable headspace oxygen analyser; company technician takes headspace oxygen readings at the bottling line using that instrument.","result":"A kinetic dataset and pathway attribution report distinguishing autoxidation from photo-oxidation, with headspace oxygen measurements from the current flush setup."},{"phase":"Phase 3 – Process change trials (months 6–9)","work":"Company implements two modified flush protocols on the existing bottling line; company technician prepares and stores trial bottles; university lab measures peroxide value, p-anisidine value, and TBARS at 30-day intervals on trial and control bottles.","result":"A comparative dataset from trial and control bottles showing peroxide value trajectories under each flush condition, and a decision on which protocol to carry forward."},{"phase":"Phase 4 – Recommendations and final report (months 10–12)","work":"University PI integrates all data and drafts implementable process recommendations; company reviews draft within 30 days and may remove confidential production details before finalisation.","result":"A final written report with ranked, implementable process recommendations and a projected shelf-life estimate for each recommended change."}],"candidate":""}
